title: A Summer of Records: How Extreme Heat is Changing Our World
subtitle: From record-breaking temperatures to rising pressure on healthcare, the global climate crisis is reshaping daily life.

summary.en: August has been confirmed as the joint-hottest month ever recorded, tying with July 2023. Scientists warn that this extreme heat is driven by the ongoing use of fossil fuels and a strengthening El Niño weather pattern. The consequences are visible globally, including damaged crops, wildfires, and increased pressure on public health systems. Experts argue that these events are not a new normal but a sign that conditions will worsen without urgent action. Governments are now facing the difficult task of adapting infrastructure to survive a future of rising temperatures.
summary.zh: 八月已被證實與二零二三年七月並列為有紀錄以來最熱的月份。科學家警告，這種極端高溫是由持續使用化石燃料以及聖嬰現象增強所驅動。其後果在全球隨處可見，包括農作物受損、野火頻發以及公共衛生系統面臨的壓力增加。專家認為，這些事件並非所謂的「新常態」，而是預示著若不採取緊急行動，情況將會持續惡化。各國政府目前正面臨艱鉅的任務，必須調整基礎設施以在未來氣溫不斷升高的環境中生存。

paragraphs.en: The world has just experienced one of its hottest periods in history. According to the European Union’s climate service, August was the joint-hottest month ever recorded, tying with July 2023. This news highlights a worrying trend: global temperatures are rising, and the consequences are being felt by communities, economies, and natural environments everywhere.
paragraphs.zh: 全球剛經歷了史上最炎熱的時期之一。根據歐盟的氣候監測機構指出，八月與二零二三年七月並列為有紀錄以來最熱的月份。這項消息凸顯了一個令人擔憂的趨勢：全球氣溫正在上升，且世界各地的社區、經濟體與自然環境都已感受到其帶來的後果。

paragraphs.en: Scientists explain that this record-breaking heat is driven by two main factors. First, the world continues to rely on fossil fuels like coal, oil, and gas, which release gases that trap heat in the atmosphere. Second, a natural climate pattern known as El Niño is currently strengthening. El Niño occurs when a part of the Pacific Ocean becomes unusually warm, releasing stored heat into the air. While this is a natural event, experts note that climate change is making it even more intense. According to the Copernicus Climate Change Service, this year’s El Niño could become one of the most powerful on record, meaning the world may see even higher temperatures in the coming year.
paragraphs.zh: 科學家解釋，這波破紀錄的高溫主要由兩大因素驅動。首先，全球仍持續依賴煤炭、石油與天然氣等化石燃料，這些燃料會釋放將熱能困在大氣層中的氣體。其次，一種稱為聖嬰現象（El Niño）的自然氣候模式目前正處於增強階段。聖嬰現象發生時，太平洋部分海域會異常升溫，並將儲存的熱能釋放到空氣中。雖然這屬於自然現象，但專家指出，氣候變遷正使其強度進一步加劇。根據哥白尼氣候變遷服務局（Copernicus Climate Change Service）的數據，今年的聖嬰現象可能成為史上最強勁的一次，這意味著全球在未來一年內可能會面臨更高的氣溫。

paragraphs.en: This heat is not just a scientific statistic; it has a real human cost. Simon Stiell, the UN climate chief, warned that the recent summer was "hot as hell," causing tens of thousands of deaths in Europe alone. He noted that the extreme weather has damaged infrastructure, forced people to leave their homes, and made it harder for businesses to operate. Beyond the immediate danger, the economic impact is massive, with costs estimated in the billions. Stiell emphasized that the climate crisis is now a major emergency for economic security, affecting everything from food prices to the cost of government borrowing.
paragraphs.zh: 這波高溫不僅是科學統計數據，更帶來了實質的人類代價。聯合國氣候變遷事務負責人史提爾（Simon Stiell）警告，剛過去的夏天「熱得像地獄」，僅在歐洲就造成數萬人死亡。他指出，極端天氣已損壞基礎設施，迫使民眾流離失所，並增加了企業營運的難度。除了直接的危險外，經濟衝擊也相當巨大，估計損失高達數十億美元。史提爾強調，氣候危機現在已成為經濟安全的一大緊急事件，影響範圍從糧食價格到政府借貸成本，無所不包。

paragraphs.en: In the United Kingdom, the impact on public services has been particularly clear. The National Health Service (NHS) reported its busiest summer ever, as five separate heatwaves pushed hospitals to their limits. According to NHS England, millions of people visited emergency departments during the summer months, a significant increase compared to previous years. Sarah Woolnough, chief executive of the King’s Fund health thinktank, stated that the NHS is now facing a "twin crisis," where summer heatwaves create as much pressure as the traditional winter peak. This leaves staff with little time to recover between busy periods.
paragraphs.zh: 在英國，極端氣候對公共服務的影響尤為明顯。英國國家醫療保健服務（NHS）報告指出，由於五波接連不斷的熱浪將醫院推向極限，這是該機構有史以來最忙碌的一個夏天。根據英格蘭國家醫療保健服務的數據，夏季期間有數百萬人前往急診室就醫，與往年相比顯著增加。醫療智庫「國王基金會」（King’s Fund）執行長伍爾諾（Sarah Woolnough）表示，國家醫療保健服務目前面臨「雙重危機」，夏季熱浪造成的壓力已與傳統冬季高峰期不相上下，這使得醫護人員在繁忙時段之間幾乎沒有喘息與恢復的空間。

paragraphs.en: Health experts point out that rising temperatures make it harder for people to breathe, especially those with existing conditions like asthma. Andrew McCracken from the charity Asthma + Lung UK explained that extreme heat, combined with wildfire smoke and pollution, creates a dangerous environment for patients. In response to these challenges, the UK government has announced plans to spend more money on hospital capacity and "heat-proofing" buildings, though some critics argue that more investment is needed to truly protect the system.
paragraphs.zh: 健康專家指出，氣溫升高使民眾呼吸變得更加困難，特別是對於患有氣喘等既有疾病的患者而言。慈善機構「英國氣喘與肺部組織」（Asthma + Lung UK）的麥克拉肯（Andrew McCracken）解釋，極端高溫加上野火煙霧與空氣污染，為患者創造了危險的環境。為了應對這些挑戰，英國政府已宣布計畫投入更多資金以提升醫院量能並為建築物進行「防熱工程」，儘管部分批評人士認為，若要真正保護醫療體系，仍需投入更多資源。

paragraphs.en: Despite these clear warnings, there is political disagreement about how to handle the crisis. Some political groups have called for slowing down policies designed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. However, Simon Stiell warned that treating climate change as a political game is a mistake. He argued that taking action is necessary to protect jobs, keep food prices affordable, and ensure community safety. He believes that being "soft" on climate action will only lead to higher costs and greater instability in the long run.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管有這些明確的警告，政界對於如何處理這場危機仍存在分歧。部分政治團體呼籲放緩旨在減少溫室氣體排放的政策。然而，史提爾警告，將氣候變遷視為政治博弈是錯誤的。他主張，採取行動對於保護就業、維持糧食價格穩定以及確保社區安全至關重要。他認為，在氣候行動上採取「軟弱」態度，長期而言只會導致更高的成本與更大的不穩定。

paragraphs.en: Researchers from Imperial College London have also rejected the idea that these extreme summers are simply the "new normal." They argue that if we continue to burn fossil fuels, these records will continue to be broken, and the weather will become even more extreme faster than we can adapt. Dr. Clair Barnes, an extreme weather researcher, noted that while the situation is serious, the future is still in our hands. How much worse the climate crisis becomes depends on the choices made today.
paragraphs.zh: 倫敦帝國學院（Imperial College London）的研究人員也反駁了這些極端夏季僅是「新常態」的說法。他們主張，如果我們繼續燃燒化石燃料，這些紀錄將會不斷被打破，天氣變化的速度將會快到讓我們無法適應。極端天氣研究員巴恩斯博士（Dr. Clair Barnes）指出，雖然情況嚴峻，但未來仍掌握在我們手中。氣候危機惡化的程度，取決於我們今日所做的選擇。

paragraphs.en: As the world looks ahead, the message from scientists and international leaders is consistent: the current path is unsustainable. With the El Niño system expected to reach its full strength later this year, the pressure on the global climate is likely to increase. Whether it is through building more resilient hospitals, changing how we produce energy, or protecting vulnerable communities, the need for urgent, coordinated action has never been clearer. The records set this summer serve as a final warning that the cost of inaction is far higher than the cost of change.
paragraphs.zh: 當世界展望未來時，科學家與國際領袖傳達的訊息是一致的：目前的發展路徑是不可持續的。隨著聖嬰系統預計在今年稍晚達到最強強度，全球氣候面臨的壓力可能會進一步增加。無論是透過打造更具韌性的醫院、改變能源生產方式，還是保護脆弱的社區，對於採取緊急且協調一致的行動之需求，從未如此明確。今年夏天創下的紀錄是一個最終警告，提醒我們不採取行動的代價，遠高於做出改變的成本。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To cause or influence something to happen or develop.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「駕駛」，這裡指導致現象發生。文中：Scientists explain that this record-breaking heat is driven by two main factors.

keyTerms.definitionEn: The time of highest activity or intensity.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（山峰），這裡指一年中業務最繁忙的時期。文中：Sarah Woolnough, chief executive of the King’s Fund health thinktank, stated that the NHS is now facing a "twin crisis," where summer heatwaves create as much pressure as the traditional winter peak.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Not strict or firm enough when dealing with a difficult situation.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「柔軟的」，這裡指對政策執行不夠堅定。文中：He believes that being "soft" on climate action will only lead to higher costs and greater instability in the long run.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A course of action or a way of behaving.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「小徑」，這裡指人類目前採取的行動方向。文中：As the world looks ahead, the message from scientists and international leaders is consistent: the current path is unsustainable.

quiz.question: According to the article, what is the primary reason the NHS in the UK is struggling to manage its workload?

options.A: It is facing a record-breaking number of patients due to a new winter virus.
options.B: The combination of summer heatwaves and traditional winter pressures leaves staff no time to recover.
options.C: The government has cut funding for emergency departments, leading to a shortage of doctors.
options.D: Wildfire smoke has forced hospitals to close their doors to the public for safety reasons.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第四段提到，NHS 經歷了有史以來最忙碌的夏天，且面臨「雙重危機」（twin crisis），即夏季熱浪帶來的壓力與傳統冬季高峰相當，導致員工在兩個繁忙時期之間幾乎沒有時間恢復。選項 A 錯誤，文中未提及冬季病毒；選項 C 錯誤，文中提到政府正計劃增加醫院容量資金，而非削減；選項 D 雖然提到了煙霧對患者的影響，但並未說醫院因此關閉。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the relationship between El Niño and climate change based on the text?

options.A: El Niño is caused entirely by human-made greenhouse gas emissions.
options.B: Climate change is a temporary phenomenon that will disappear once El Niño ends.
options.C: Climate change is amplifying the intensity of a naturally occurring weather pattern.
options.D: El Niño is the main reason why global temperatures are rising, regardless of fossil fuel use.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第二段說明 El Niño 是一種自然氣候模式，但專家指出氣候變遷正在使其變得更加強烈。這顯示氣候變遷與自然現象產生了加乘效果。選項 A 錯誤，El Niño 是自然現象；選項 B 錯誤，氣候變遷並非暫時現象；選項 D 錯誤，文中強調化石燃料與 El Niño 同為導致高溫的因素，而非僅有後者。

quiz.question: In the phrase 'being "soft" on climate action', what does the word 'soft' imply?

options.A: Lacking the necessary firmness or strictness to achieve effective results.
options.B: Being physically gentle and comfortable to the touch.
options.C: Having a flexible plan that can be easily changed at any time.
options.D: Showing kindness and sympathy toward those who oppose climate policies.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在第六段中，Simon Stiell 警告對氣候行動採取「soft」（軟弱的/不嚴格的）態度會導致長期成本增加與不穩定。這裡的 soft 指的是缺乏決心或嚴格執行力的政策。選項 B 是字面意義，在此不適用；選項 C 雖然提到靈活性，但與文意中的「消極怠惰」不符；選項 D 誤解了語境，文中並未強調對反對者的同情。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article regarding the current climate situation?

options.A: The world must focus solely on building more resilient hospitals to survive future summers.
options.B: Extreme weather is the 'new normal' and humans must learn to adapt to it without changing energy habits.
options.C: Political disagreement is the only obstacle preventing the world from solving the climate crisis.
options.D: Urgent and coordinated action is necessary because the cost of doing nothing outweighs the cost of change.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。文章最後一段總結了科學家與國際領袖的共識，強調目前的道路是不可持續的，必須採取緊急且協調的行動，因為「不作為的代價遠高於改變的代價」。選項 A 太過侷限於醫療層面；選項 B 與文中第七段研究人員的觀點相反；選項 C 雖然提到了政治分歧，但並非文章唯一的重點，也非解決問題的全部。
